angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,205,648 km at 14.53 pc = 1.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 126660: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 68.83 +/- 0.14 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 14.529 +/- 0.03 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 69.0686 +/- 0.1579 mas (same row, RUWE 3.38), 437.5 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 1.733 +/- 0.011 solar radii from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 126660: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.109 +/- 0.007 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 1.733 +/- 0.011 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 1,205,648 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.232 +/- 0.058 solar masses from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 126660: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.232 +/- 0.058 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6265 +/- 41 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 126660: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 6265 +/- 41 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 126660: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 6265 +/- 41 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/theta-bootis.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.051, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
